doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Scott LaFaro's fatal crash near Geneva
summary: His dad told him about LaFaro and showed the 1961 newspaper; he describes the crash site and LaFaro's night with Stan Getz.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: That’s right I forgot he came from there.
I’m sort of getting off into—
Well I played guitar and then I got interested in bass, I got interested in jazz.

And then my dad told me about Scott LaFaro, who he knew very well, having come from Geneva, Scott. And he showed me the newspaper article, the cover page on the Geneva Times from 1961, July 6, 1961 where LaFaro is on the cover, with his crashed car and the whole bit.

Flint, New York, just between 5 and 20, between Geneva and Canandaigua. And the tree — I was just there a few months ago — the tree is still there, scarred, sitting in front of this little house. My first lesson I drove by it, knowing what it was.

He’d been up all night, he worked the night with Stan Getz in I believe it was either Newport or Lake Placid. I think he had the gig in Newport, which there’s recorded evidence with Stan Getz. I haven’t heard it — all you people out there, I’d like to hear it — and he either stayed up and drove to Geneva or there was another gig the night after that and then he stayed up all night and drove to Geneva. My dad saw him, blah, blah, blah, didn’t accompany him that night.
